definition: Model Governance and Compliance is a core concept in AI Engineering. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Model Governance and Compliance is
theory.body: Model Governance and Compliance describes the methods and patterns used within AI Engineering to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Model Governance and Compliance is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Model Governance and Compliance matters
theory.body: Without Model Governance and Compliance, systems built with AI Engineering are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Model Governance and Compliance works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Model Governance and Compliance follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Model Governance and Compliance.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Model Governance and Compliance
theory.body: Model Governance and Compliance offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
